title: Multi-Process Concurrency Probe

falsificationCriterionStatedBeforeTheRun.where: FALSIFICATION_CRITERIA in packages/mcp-server/test/probes/concurrency-probe.ts, printed to stdout by --run BEFORE any process is spawned
falsificationCriterionStatedBeforeTheRun.howItIsBindingRatherThanDecorative: Each of the five criteria maps one-to-one onto a field of ConcurrencyVerdict that the blocking test asserts is empty. There is no criterion without a field and no field without a criterion, so the probe cannot quietly narrow what would have counted as failure after seeing the result.
criteria: REUSE — the same Sequence value appears on two rows of the tenant's durable JSONL mirror. One occurrence refutes the monotonicity claim outright.
LOST WRITE — a Sequence a writer reported as committed is absent from the durable mirror (matched by row identity, not by Sequence, so one defect cannot manufacture a second).

REGRESSION ACROSS REBUILD — a Sequence allocated after rebuildFromJsonl is at or below the highest Sequence allocated before it. eap_sequences is deliberately excluded from the tables a rebuild purges precisely so this cannot happen.
GAP — the durable Sequences are not the contiguous range 1..n. A Sequence consumed by a transaction whose row is not durable is a lost write with the allocator itself as witness.
DUPLICATE IDENTITY — one row identifier appears twice in the durable mirror, meaning a transaction's mirror append survived a rollback its SQLite half did not.

topology.connectionsExplanation: One connection per writer process, opened by that process through the same openDb(stateDir/state.sqlite) call state.ts uses to start a real host, plus the parent's own connection used for the rebuild.
topology.processesAreReal: Each writer is a separate OS process spawned by spawnProbeProcess with stdout and stderr on a FILE DESCRIPTOR, never a pipe (task 14 measured that piping a spawned Bun process's stdout makes the Windows EBUSY teardown race fire reliably: 2/2 piped runs failed, 0/4 with an fd). The blocking test asserts the four reported pids are distinct and none is the parent's.
topology.whyFourAndTwelve: Four writers on an 8-core reference machine keeps three processes queued behind the lock holder at every moment — the condition the probe exists to create — without oversubscribing the machine so far that the timings measure the scheduler. Twelve writes each is 48 serialised lock acquisitions per phase; a single-digit count leaves the outcome decidable by one lucky interleaving, and a four-figure count buys no additional interleaving class at ten times the wall cost.
topology.phaseStructure: Writers are spawned ONCE and live across both phases on file barriers. Phase A: 4x12 concurrent writes. Then the parent rebuilds from JSONL on its own connection while all four writer connections are still open. Phase B: 4x12 concurrent writes, and phase B is where the write-lock hold is measured. Reusing the processes is both cheaper (4 spawns, not 8) and more faithful — a real host does not reconnect after a rebuild, so phase B's connections were already open when the rebuild ran.
topology.barrier: Every writer publishes a ready file, parks on a barrier file, and is released together — so the write lock is contested from the first transaction rather than from the tenth.

blockingAssertions: no reused Sequence in the durable mirror
no duplicate row identifier in the durable mirror
no admitted write absent from the durable mirror
no post-rebuild Sequence at or below the pre-rebuild maximum
no gap in the durable Sequence range
4 distinct writer pids, none of them the parent's, and 5 connections
all four writers loaded the same db.ts (identical sha256) and that allocator advances (signature[1] === signature[0] + 1)
howTheSeparationIsENFORCEDRatherThanInte: TYPE WALL: analyzeConcurrency takes ConcurrencyObservation, a type that has NO timing field of any kind. The timings live on a separate ConcurrencyTimings value that the analyser's signature cannot accept. A verdict cannot be a function of a duration even by accident, because a duration cannot be expressed in the analyser's input type.

REGRESSION TEST ON THE VERDICT SHAPE: a test asserts the verdict object carries no key containing ms/duration/elapsed/wall/hold/latency/starvation, so a later edit that smuggles a timing into the verdict fails there rather than quietly creating a timing gate.

LEDGER REFUSAL ONE LAYER DOWN: recordSample is the only sink for the timings, and benchmark-ledger.ts refuses any sample carrying expected/bound/asserted/threshold/budget/limit, and any sample naming an EAP-XXX-NNN identifier anywhere in its JSON.
NO BAND DECLARED: a band is a bound. None of the three metrics is banded, so nothing in the repository compares these numbers to a threshold at all.
blockingVersusLedgerOnly.starvationDefinition: Slowest writer's phase-B wall time divided by the fastest writer's, where every writer ran an IDENTICAL quota of identical work — so the whole difference is time spent waiting behind another writer's lock and nothing else. 1.0 is perfect fairness. Recorded and never asserted: SQLite promises fairness on no platform, this repository has taken no decision about acceptable service under contention, and a bound harvested from one laptop under unknown ambient load is exactly the measurement-dressed-as-assertion task 08 exists to catch.
blockingVersusLedgerOnly.ledgerAppendSerialisation: appendToLedger takes NO LOCK (task 16 weak spot W7). Only the coordinating parent records, only after every child has exited, and every writer child sets EAP_PROBE_CONCURRENCY_WRITER as its first statement so assertSoleLedgerWriter() REFUSES any append from inside a writer. The three appends are three sequential synchronous calls in one process.

acceptance3.rule: Per F002's mutation rule (five no-op mutations have been scored as passes in this feature, twice by the orchestrator), every break below was independently proved to have reached the code under probe BEFORE any conclusion was drawn from the probe's output.
independentProofMechanism: SOURCE DIGEST: each writer child hashes the packages/mcp-server/src/db.ts it loaded and reports the sha256. A break that did not move that digest did not reach the child.

BEHAVIOURAL SIGNATURE: each writer takes two consecutive allocations on a scratch tenant before the barrier and reports the pair. The unbroken allocator yields [1,2]. This witnesses the loaded implementation's behaviour, not merely the bytes on disk.
GIT: db.ts sha256 was 36d79f2da63f54a0e2f2797aecb97ec6a32d5160860562dcb076a294ac899ecd before every break and identical after every revert; git status --porcelain shows db.ts unmodified.

breaks.what: ON CONFLICT(tenant_id, name) DO UPDATE SET value = value + 1  ->  DO UPDATE SET value = value
breaks.proofItTookEffect: db.ts sha256 moved 36d79f2d... -> e8822045...; the behavioural signature reported by every writer became [1,1] instead of [1,2].
breaks.probeReported: REFUTED — 1 REUSED Sequence(s): 1; 48 post-rebuild Sequence(s) at or below the pre-rebuild maximum 1.

breaks.what: The counter UPSERT replaced with SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq),0)+1 FROM contestations WHERE tenant_id = ? — the exact pattern db.ts's comment says the allocator replaced.
breaks.proofItTookEffect: db.ts sha256 moved 36d79f2d... -> b6806bdf...; the behavioural signature became [1,1].
breaks.probeReported: SURVIVED — 96 durable write(s), no Sequence reuse, no lost admitted write, no regression across the rebuild. The DURABLE-RECORD VERDICT DID NOT CATCH THIS.
breaks.blockingTest: FAILED, but only on the auxiliary behavioural-signature assertion, not on any falsification criterion.
breaks.whyThisMatters: serialTransaction already takes the write lock at BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so the read-decide-write race MAX+1 is vulnerable to never opens; and a JSONL rebuild REPLAYS the rows, so the table maximum is restored and a table-derived allocator does not regress either. What the durable counter uniquely defends against is reuse after ROW DELETION, and no path this probe drives deletes rows. STATED CONSEQUENCE: this probe proves the allocator does not reuse or lose under multi-process contention and across a rebuild; it does NOT prove the counter design is necessary.

breaks.what: eap_sequences added to ALL_TABLES, so the rebuild wipes the durable allocator — the exact failure db.ts's own comment says the exclusion exists to prevent.
breaks.probeReported: REFUTED — 48 REUSED Sequence(s): 1..48; 48 post-rebuild Sequence(s) at or below the pre-rebuild maximum 48.
breaks.whyThisMatters: This is the property the probe uniquely tests, it is caught by the DURABLE RECORD rather than by an auxiliary witness, and no other test in this repository exercises it.

probeSelfMutations.rule: The probe's own detectors were mutated to confirm they are load-bearing. Each mutation's effect on the file the test imports was proved by sha256 before the run, and the file was restored bit-identical (13ed31e2...) afterwards.
results: M1 assertSoleLedgerWriter guard neutralised (if (false)) -> 'a writer child is REFUSED the ledger' FAILED.
M2 starvationRatio returns 1 always -> 'an overtaken writer reports its factor' FAILED.

M4 rebuild-regression detector blinded (<= -> <) -> 'a post-rebuild Sequence at or below the pre-rebuild maximum REFUTES the allocator's survival' FAILED.

dbTs.why: The probe observes the allocator entirely from outside: the writers call the public openDb / serialTransaction / allocateSequence / write surface, and the evidence is the tenant's durable JSONL mirror read from disk after every writer process exited. No lock-hold instrumentation was needed inside production code, because the interval a write lock is held IS the interval of the serialTransaction call the probe itself makes, and it can be timed from the caller. Per the task's own preference, this is the better outcome and it is stated explicitly.
dbTs.consequenceForCoverage: Coverage did not move. An instrumented run reproduced 2994/3257 lines and 223/245 functions exactly. db.ts is in any case outside the declared coverage scope (packages/client/src/eap.ts, packages/graph-core/src/eap, packages/mcp-server/src/eap, gates.ts, tools/eap.ts).

adr0021Compliance: Verification by the durable record, never self-report. The writers report which Sequences they believe they committed — that is the CLAIM. The evidence is the tenant's durable JSONL mirror (which db.ts calls the truth, SQLite being the derived index), read by the parent after every writer has exited. Reuse is caught in the mirror, never in a writer's opinion of itself; the writers' claims are only ever used as the set the durable record must CONTAIN.

ledgerSamplesAppended.whyUnbanded: Three samples is below MIN_BAND_WINDOW (5), and a band on a contention timing taken on one shared developer machine would be authoring a bound out of an unknown ambient load. The metrics are NOT labelled QA6 or QA7 either: neither family is about write-lock contention, and mislabelling them to buy the may-not-be-banded exemption would be a lie that bought a convenience. They are honestly an unbanded gap in the ledger's own words, and the ledger prints that on every check.
ledgerSamplesAppended.observationWorthAttention: The p50 (0.946 / 0.947 / 0.942 ms) and the MAX (47.904 / 47.671 / 48.336 ms) are both stable to within a millisecond across three independent runs. A ~48 ms tail that recurs that precisely is not jitter — it looks like a fixed cost, plausibly a WAL checkpoint, and deserves someone's attention. This probe records it and claims nothing about it.

decisionsOwnedAndTaken.runsInSuite: YES, at 4 writers x 12 writes, on every bun test run. Measured cost: the probe test file completes in ~1.5 s and the full suite moved from ~81 s to 83.1 s (about 2%). A separate invocation nobody wires up was rejected: a probe that runs only when someone remembers proves nothing about the commit that broke the thing. RECORDING is not in the suite — recordSample appends only under EAP_BENCHMARK_RECORD, so an ordinary bun test measures, reports, and dirties no committed file. When CI records is task 20's.
decisionsOwnedAndTaken.windowsVersusLinux: The correctness half rests on SQLite transaction semantics, not on the platform's locking primitives (LockFileEx versus POSIX advisory locks), so it is identical and fully meaningful on both. The timing half is not comparable across the two and nothing tries to compare it: os is a fingerprint component, so Windows and Linux samples are different ledger partitions and are never pooled. There is no OS on which this probe is quietly the weaker check. RESIDUAL: it has only ever been RUN on Windows; the starvation ratio near 5 may be a Windows handoff artefact and the first Linux run is the experiment.

hostTsChanges.what: Extracted spawnProbeProcess (bun <args> with stdout and stderr on a file descriptor, never a pipe) and added waitForPath. spawnProbeHost now goes through spawnProbeProcess, so exactly one place in the repository decides the no-pipe rule.
hostTsChanges.why: The probe needs to spawn writers, not hosts, with the same discipline and for the same measured reason. Writing a second private spawn in the probe was the obvious way to reintroduce the pipe task 14 measured.
hostTsChanges.behaviourChange: None. spawnProbeHost's ready-file handshake, timeout, error text and teardown are unchanged; only the spawn call and the exitCode accessor moved.

weakSpots: THE GAP AND DUPLICATE IDENTITY CRITERIA HAVE NEVER FIRED, in any real or broken run. They are pinned by unit tests over synthetic observations only — asserted but unwitnessed.

BREAK-2 IS A REAL BLIND SPOT: the durable-record verdict cannot distinguish the counter-based allocator from a serialised MAX+1 allocator, because BEGIN IMMEDIATE already removes the race and a rebuild replays the rows. Closing it needs a real row-deletion path — capability_executions has one (retention DELETEs oldest by ordinal, and its ordinal comes from allocateSequence) — and that is not owned by this task.

removeStateDir WARNS ON ESSENTIALLY EVERY RUN of this probe (Windows holds SQLite/WAL handles after five processes exit), so the probe leaves temp directories behind. By design it warns rather than throws; the practical effect is litter in TMPDIR that nothing cleans.
THE THREE METRICS ARE UNBANDED, which the ledger itself reports as a gap for any metric outside a quarantined family. Deliberate, but it means the ledger currently asserts nothing about them.

THE PROBE DRIVES db.ts DIRECTLY, not a running MCP host over transport. Each writer's connection is the connection a host would have (same openDb call), so the concurrency is faithful, but the guarantee proven is the db-layer one, not the tool-layer one.
ONLY WINDOWS HAS EVER RUN IT.
foundButNotOwned: reconcile-traceability.ts decides EAP Test Corpus membership by a RAW SUBSTRING SCAN of a test file's bytes for the annotation import path, so a file that merely MENTIONS that path in a comment is enrolled in the corpus. This probe's test file was enrolled purely because its header explained why it is NOT in the corpus, which failed the 'declares the corpus' test and would have moved the committed unclaimed-test-case baseline. Worked around by rewording the comment so it cannot name the path — a fragile fix to a fragile rule. A real fix reads import statements rather than bytes. Out of scope here.
A ~48 ms recurring maximum write-lock hold that is stable to within a millisecond across runs. Recorded, not diagnosed.

environmentalDegradationFoundDuringTheFi.what: Partway through this task the reference machine became roughly 3-4x slower and STAYED slow. The full suite went from 83 s to 295-345 s. Twelve tests that are bounded by a 5 s or 10 s timeout — the QA-7 target-repo tests against C:\Users\User\Documents\harness-kit, plus the live SSE/drift tests — began failing on timeout, reproducibly, on every run.
provedNotCausedByThisTask: Nothing outside packages/mcp-server/test/probes imports the probe or the probe harness (grep over packages and scripts).
The failures reproduce when target-repo-scale.test.ts is run ALONE, in its own process, where none of this task's code is ever loaded.
All 7 of that file's tests PASS unchanged under `bun test --timeout 90000` (74.97 s for 7 tests, about 10 s each — they used to fit inside 5 s). It is slowness, not breakage.
The target repo itself is unchanged: 327 files, nothing modified in the last 3 hours, `git status --porcelain` empty.
environmentalDegradationFoundDuringTheFi.notFixedNotSuppressed: No timeout was raised in any committed file, no test was skipped or weakened, and nothing was marked flaky. The slowdown is a property of this machine right now and is reported rather than worked around.
environmentalDegradationFoundDuringTheFi.howAGREENVERIFYWASOBTAINEDHONESTLY: These 12 tests are guarded by targetRepoAvailable() and SKIP when the target repo is absent — which is the condition CI actually runs in (ubuntu-latest has no such path), and which task 15 already recorded as producing an IDENTICAL coverage figure. Running `bun run verify` and `coverage-gate.ts` with OG_TARGET_REPO pointed at a nonexistent path reproduces the CI configuration exactly: 1072 pass / 20 skip / 1 todo / 0 fail, exit 0, and coverage 2994/3257 and 223/245 reproduced exactly. Both results are reported below; neither is presented as the other.

pendingCiGates.note: Task 20 owns CI topology. Nothing in .github was touched by this task.
newThisTask: The concurrency probe runs inside bun test already, so it needs no separate CI job. It adds ~2 s to every suite run and ~4 extra OS processes.

RECORDING to the Benchmark Ledger is still opt-in (EAP_BENCHMARK_RECORD). If CI is ever wired to record, it MUST NOT run two recording probes concurrently — appendToLedger takes no lock and concurrent appends seal against the same chain head and corrupt a committed append-only file. A recording CI step must be serial, and ideally a single job.
The probe has never been run on Linux. The first CI run on ubuntu-latest is the experiment; if the correctness half fails there it is a genuine finding, not a flake, and must not be re-run away.
